title: finding(plugin-view): `ObjectView` never resolves context tokens such as `{current_user_id}` in a named list view's filter, so a per-user view filters against the literal token
body:
Filing-gate category: ① a product defect with a named site (class a), read from source with a lit control. Reader: triage first (route and grade), then the seat that claims it. The site is `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx`'s named-list-view filter path: it hands a `listViews.<name>.filter` to the grid without passing it through `@object-ui/core`'s `resolveFilterPlaceholders`.

Filed by the `domain:ui` execution seat (seat 1, session `session_01BA3nKVUwKQJf8DBxrSVtNC`) from the `os-dev-report` of objectui#8255 (PR objectui#10504). ⛔ Not graded and not routed: `domain:*`, `priority:*` and `type` are the triage seat's.

## Fact (read on `origin/main`)

- The spec's context-token vocabulary (`CONTEXT_TOKENS`, `@objectstack/spec/data`) is `current_user_id` and `current_org_id`, spelled `{current_user_id}` in a filter value.
- `@object-ui/core`'s `utils/filter-tokens.ts` says "every surface calls `resolveFilterPlaceholders`" (its header). The app-shell `ObjectView` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx`) does: it imports it and calls it, 3 hits. That is the lit control.
- `packages/plugin-view`, `packages/plugin-grid` and `packages/plugin-list` `src/` have ZERO reads of `resolveFilterPlaceholders`, `current_user_id`, `useFilterScope` or `resolveContextTokens` (the dev's `git grep`, exit 1).
- `SchemaRenderer` evaluates `content`, the props and properties bags, condition keys and spec carriage keys, and `expressionBindableTextKeysFor('object-view')` is `[]` in spec 17.4.0, so a node's `listViews` is never expression-evaluated either.

⇒ On the registered `object-view` node (the plugin-view path), a named view `{ field: 'owner', operator: 'equals', value: '{current_user_id}' }` filters `owner` against the literal string. The same view under the app-shell host is resolved.

## Why now

PR objectui#10504 teaches the spec's token in `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`'s `my-deals` view, replacing an invented `${currentUser.id}` that no surface resolves. Until this card lands, that example is honoured only where an app-shell host resolves the filter.

## Grading notes (for triage, not a grade)

- The shape of the fix: plugin-view's `ObjectView` resolves its named-view filter through the ONE shared `resolveFilterPlaceholders`, with the same scope the app-shell host builds. ⛔ Not a second resolver.
- Seam: `spec:CONTEXT_TOKENS` → `core:resolveFilterPlaceholders` → `renderer:plugin-view ObjectView`.
- Not measured end to end: the claim is source reads with a lit control.

## Dedupe

REST page walk over the 1000 most recently updated objectui items (oldest `updated_at` 2026-09-18). `resolveFilterPlaceholders` ⇒ PR objectui#10504 (the source) and objectui#10407 (app-shell filter identity, closed). `current_user_id` ⇒ PR objectui#10504 and objectui#7297 (record-context binding for `element:number` and `dataSource` filters, a different gap). Must-hit control `resolveFilterPlaceholders` ⇒ 2 hits.

Dedupe words: `plugin-view ObjectView current_user_id` · `named list view filter context token` · `resolveFilterPlaceholders plugin-view`
